name: Lateral approach to the 5th metatarsal
aliases: lateral approach to the fifth metatarsal base
corridor: Lateral incision at the dorsal-plantar skin junction along the fifth metatarsal, protecting the sural nerve branches and short saphenous vein, elevating abductor digiti minimi to expose the bone

positioning.text: Position supine with a bump under the ipsilateral hip so the lateral foot is presented, under tourniquet control.

surface_landmarks.text: Identify the styloid process of the base of the fifth metatarsal and the dorsal-plantar skin junction.

incision.text: Start just proximal to the styloid process at the junction of dorsal and plantar skin and extend distally as far as required.

superficial_interval.text: Identify and protect the branches of the sural nerve and the short saphenous vein, which lie subcutaneously in the line of the approach.

deep_interval.text: Expose and longitudinally incise the fascia over the abductor digiti minimi, retracting the muscle plantarward and the skin dorsally with Langenbeck retractors to reach the bone.

layers.text: Skin, subcutaneous tissue with sural nerve branches and short saphenous vein, abductor digiti minimi, and the fifth metatarsal.

structures_at_risk.text: The branches of the sural nerve and the short saphenous vein are at risk in the line of the incision.

danger_zones.text: The subcutaneous lateral border is the danger zone for the sural nerve and short saphenous vein.

retraction_hazards.text: Use Langenbeck retractors and keep the sural nerve and vein out of the retractor.

exposure.text: Exposes the base and shaft of the fifth metatarsal.

limitations.text: The sural nerve and short saphenous vein limit the safe subcutaneous dissection.

indications.text: Indicated for fixation of fifth metatarsal fractures.

closure.text: Perform subcuticular closure with resorbable sutures and close skin with nylon.

complications.text: Complications include sural nerve injury with lateral foot numbness or neuroma and wound problems.

procedure_applications.condition: A fifth metatarsal fracture, including a base or Jones fracture, is fixed

questions.question: Where does the lateral fifth metatarsal incision lie relative to the skin?
questions.answer: At the junction of the dorsal and plantar skin.

questions.question: Which two structures lie subcutaneously in the line of this approach?
questions.answer: Branches of the sural nerve and the short saphenous vein.

questions.question: Which muscle fascia is incised to reach the bone?
questions.answer: The fascia over the abductor digiti minimi.
